conviction_note: Fundamentals lean to a small shortfall (peer deposit costs rose 5-10bp in Q3 against a 2.75% NIM guide set in July, the Sept 16 Fed hike sits on the Q4 2.80% guide, and a 4-analyst $0.87 consensus is $0.01-0.03 above the guide arithmetic), but a 7.3%-of-float short with 11.5 days to cover, a stock already 6% lower in 20 sessions and 2.6 points behind KRE, Hold targets at spot and the nearest Massachusetts peer (INDB) bought +3.6% on an in-line print keep p_up near 50; findings sum -2.4 while the scaled number is -0.6 because the negatives are proxies and inferences and the positioning is a mechanism of its own.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS consensus $0.87 from 4 analysts (Benzinga https://www.benzinga.com/quote/WASH/earnings-forecasts and AAII 2026-10-17 https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/516804-what-you-need-to-know-about-washington-trust-bancorp-incs-q3-earnings, agreeing); revenue consensus $62.5m (Benzinga only). Company guide from the 2026-07-21 call: Q3 NIM about 2.75%, Q4 about 2.80%, Q3 noninterest expense just under $39m, FY tax rate about 21.5% (https://www.webull.com/news/15265414580347904).
positioning_check: Short interest 1,381,186 shares = 7.34% of float, 11.5 days to cover, FINRA record date 2026-09-30 published 2026-10-09, down 0.74% from 1,391,472 on 2026-09-15 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/WASH/short-interest/). Option chain unusable in the sealed baseline (39 contracts total OI, put/call OI 0.15, skew null); Unusual Whales shows an implied earnings move of +/-9.58% on 2026-10-19 (https://unusualwhales.com/stock/WASH/earnings) and +/-8.9% on 2026-10-06. Price: WASH 39.16 (Sep 21) to 36.72 (Oct 19) = -6.2% over 20 sessions vs KRE 71.99 to 69.39 = -3.6% (Yahoo chart v8, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/WASH?range=2mo&interval=1d and .../KRE); WASH fell 2.2% on the Fed hike day (Sep 16) vs KRE -1.8%. Sell-side: KBW Hold $36 (2026-07-21), Piper Sandler Hold $35 (2026-06-26), Seaport downgraded Buy to Hold 2026-07-22 (https://www.investing.com/equities/washington-trust-consensus-estimates). No skew to read; the crowded short argues for shrinking any negative.

findings.finding: Three Northeast banks that reported after WASH last spoke all printed rising Q3 deposit costs: INDB total cost of deposits 1.42% (+6bp QoQ, interest-bearing +8bp), Citizens interest-bearing deposit cost 2.13% (+5bp) with total deposits down $0.4bn, M&T interest-bearing deposit cost 2.05% (+10bp); WASH's own Q2 interest-bearing deposit cost was 2.41% (down 1bp QoQ) and its 2.75% Q3 NIM guide was given on 2026-07-21 on the premise that funding costs were still easing ('FHLB advances have mostly repriced down, a little bit left to go').
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The NIM line is what this name trades on: Q1 2026 (NIM 2.63%, EPS $0.66 vs $0.77) -16.9%; Q2 2026 (NIM 2.73%, +10bp, EPS $0.83 vs $0.77) +8.15%; Q4 2025 +12.69% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The $0.87 consensus has moved only one up/one down revision in the past month (AAII, 2026-10-17) and still implies NII roughly $1m above Q2, which needs the full 2.75%; if the market had priced a deposit-cost drift of 5-8bp on $4.6bn of interest-bearing deposits (about $0.6-0.9m a quarter, 4-6bp of NIM) the consensus would sit at $0.84-0.85 and the KBW/Piper Hold targets would have moved below spot.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a company number. Three independent primary documents point the same way: Citizens Q3 2026 review (https://finsee.ai/earnings/cfg/2026/q3/en/, 2026-10-16) and M&T's Q3 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000036270/000003627026000057/ex991release3q26.htm, 2026-10-15). Shares the Q2 release and call transcript with finding 5.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 (12-0), after the Q4 NIM guide of about 2.80% was given on 2026-07-21; WASH has $745m of time deposits at a 3.38% weighted rate and $220m of FHLB advances at 3.98% maturing by year-end, so the Q4 repricing that the 2.80% guide relied on now rolls into a higher short rate, and the Oct 20 call is the first chance to hold or trim that guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2.75%/2.80% guide was part of the Q2 print bought +8.15% (2026-07-20); the Q1 print with no margin relief in sight sold -16.9%. The market sold WASH 2.2% on hike day against KRE -1.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: The hike itself is priced (WASH -6.2% over 20 sessions, 2.6 points behind KRE), but the guide is not: no analyst action since the hike (last actions 2026-07-21/22), and the consensus still carries the pre-hike margin path. If the market expected a trimmed Q4 guide the 2027 estimates and targets would have moved after Sept 16; they did not.
findings.independence: Inference (macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by the company). Maturity schedules from the Q2 10-Q R67 and R69 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/737468/000073746826000114/R67.htm, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/737468/000073746826000114/R69.htm, filed 2026-08-06). Management's own counterweight on the Q2 call: a steeper curve helps new production and loan amortisation is a tailwind. Shares the rate mechanism with finding 1 but a different line (Q4 guide vs Q3 print).

findings.finding: Credit overhang disclosed but unresolved: $28.9m of CRE office is on nonaccrual and 90+ days past due (a $22.3m Class A loan plus $6.6m of lab space), the $34.5m lab-space book carries a 103% loan-to-value with all of it criticized ($27.9m special mention, $6.6m classified), a $3.75m Class B special-mention office loan matured in Q3, and the ACL is 0.83% of loans with ACL/nonaccrual at 107% and no specific reserve disclosed; any Q3 resolution (charge-off, payoff, or further migration) prints straight through provision.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: $29.1m added to nonaccrual, provision $4.0m, stock -16.9%. Q2 2026: provision back to $1.6m, net charge-offs $55k, stock +8.15%. INDB rose 3.6% on 2026-10-16 despite a new office nonperformer with a specific reserve, so the peer tape is not punishing a contained office credit.
findings.why_not_priced: Two-sided and largely known: the nonaccrual office loan and the lab-space LTV were in the Q1 and Q2 releases and the stock recovered 8% in July, so a status-quo quarter is in the price; what is not priced is the direction of resolution, and a charge-off of 20-30% on $28.9m ($6-9m) would be 4-6x the Q2 provision, while a payoff would release the overhang. Sized small net of the rest of the book (consumer and C&I charge-offs near zero, C&I special mention down to $2.0m).
findings.independence: Risk-rating detail from the Q2 10-Q R53 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/737468/000073746826000114/R53.htm, 2026-08-06): CRE classified $35.0m vs $6.2m at Dec 31, 2025; CRE special mention $47.5m vs $63.3m. Class B maturity from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15265414580347904, 2026-07-21). No Rhode Island office default news found for Q3.

findings.finding: Positioning is set up for a squeeze on an in-line print: 7.34% of float short with 11.5 days to cover (record 2026-09-30), the stock down 6.2% over 20 sessions versus KRE -3.6% and sitting at the Hold targets ($35 Piper, $36 KBW), while the nearest Massachusetts peer INDB rose 3.6% on 2026-10-16 on a flat core NIM with higher deposit costs and a new office nonperformer.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been bought hard on this name (+8.15%, +12.69%); the last three prints averaged a 12.6% absolute move against a 7-print median of 3.56%, and options price about 9.6% (thin chain).
findings.why_not_priced: If the market had positioned for a squeeze, short interest would have fallen into the print (it was flat, 1.39m to 1.38m) and the stock would not have underperformed KRE by 2.6 points over the run-in with no company news; the drift happened on ordinary volume (avg 113k shares) with no filing since the Aug 14 shelf effectiveness.
findings.independence: Price series from Yahoo chart v8 (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/INDB?range=1mo&interval=1d, INDB 77.08 on Oct 15 to 79.88 on Oct 16; CFG flat -0.1% on its Oct 16 print; MTB -1.5% on Oct 16). Targets from investing.com (https://www.investing.com/equities/washington-trust-consensus-estimates). Positive sign cuts against findings 1, 2 and 5; both can be true (a small miss into a crowded short is the lesson-7 case).

findings.finding: The $0.87 consensus sits $0.01-0.03 above what management's own guide arithmetic produces: NII at 2.75% NIM on about $6.2bn of earning assets for 92 days is about $42.9m (+$1.1m QoQ), expenses guided to just under $39m (+$1m), the $265k of seasonal tax-servicing wealth fees in Q2 do not recur, so pre-provision income is roughly $22.1m versus $21.9m in Q2 and EPS lands near $0.84-0.86 with the Q2 provision ($1.6m) repeated.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS versus consensus is the line this stock pays on: $0.66 vs $0.77 gave -16.9% (2026-04-20), $0.83 vs $0.77 gave +8.15% (2026-07-20).
findings.why_not_priced: A 4-analyst bar that has been revised one up and one down in the past month (AAII 2026-10-17) shows nobody has redone the arithmetic since the guide; if they had, the consensus would read $0.85, which is where the guide puts it. Inside the guided range on NIM and expenses, so this is a reported-quarter item rather than new information; sized small for that.
findings.independence: Average-balance and income-statement detail from the Q2 2026 release (https://s202.q4cdn.com/917433312/files/doc_news/Washington-Trust-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results-2026.pdf, 2026-07-20: avg earning assets $6,174m, NII $41.8m, noninterest expense $38.6m, provision $1.6m, diluted shares 19.2m). Consensus from Benzinga and AAII (two agreeing sources). Shares the Q2 call with finding 1; the two differ in that this one assumes the guide is hit.

findings.finding: Wealth management (60% of noninterest income, $11.2m in Q2 on $7.92bn AUA, 91% managed) gets a modest market tailwind: the S&P 500 rose about 2.0-2.3% in Q3 2026 (First Citizens: +2%; Novel Investor: +2.3%), so asset-based fees should rise low-single digits QoQ, roughly in line with what the $0.87 bar needs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Wealth fees have not been the swing line in any of the last three reactions; Q2's +5% wealth growth was a secondary mention in the +8.15% print.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: index levels are public and the Q2 AUA base is in the release; filed small because a consensus that is slightly above the guide needs this line to deliver.
findings.independence: Proxy (index return to fee revenue). First Citizens Q3 2026 market review (https://www.firstcitizens.com/content/dam/firstcitizens/pdfs/wealth/market-outlook/2026/q3-2026-quarterly-market-review.pdf) agrees on about +2%. AUA base from the Q2 release.

findings.finding: Mortgage banking ($3.47m in Q2, +14% on $216m of originations, 63% originated for sale) faces a weaker Q3 backdrop: the MBA 30-year conforming rate reached 6.65% in the week of July 10, 2026, its highest since August 2025, with total applications down 2.7% and purchase applications tumbling, while WASH's June 30 pipeline was $121m against $216m of Q2 originations.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Mortgage banking has not driven any of the last three reactions; it is 5-6% of revenue.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and seasonal; nobody models this line on a 4-analyst name. Filed because the bar is tight and the Q2 mortgage figure was flattered by spring volume.
findings.independence: Proxy (national MBA series, July only; the September 2026 MBA weeks could not be found in this turn). Pipeline figure from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15265414580347904). Refinance share was rising (43.2%) in the same MBA week, which partly offsets.

findings.finding: A new $150m universal shelf (S-3 filed 2026-08-07, effective 2026-08-14: common, preferred, debt, warrants, units; proceeds 'general corporate purposes'; no ATM or sales agent named) replaces the shelf declared effective 2023-09-29 that funded the December 2024 $55m underwritten equity raise for a securities repositioning; with AOCI at -$77m and the $885m securities book yielding 3.44% against 5.20% on loans, the shelf makes a second repositioning possible, but nothing is announced and CET1 is 11.89%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved reaction on this line in the baseline window; the December 2024 raise predates the 7 prints carried.
findings.why_not_priced: Asked what the money buys: nothing visible. The timing fits a routine three-year renewal (prior shelf effective 2023-09-29, three-year life to 2026-09), there is no prospectus supplement, no 8-K and capital is strong, so this is sized at near zero and filed so the panel can see it; it would matter only if the Oct 19 release announces a repositioning.
findings.independence: Prior shelf history from the 2023 S-3 and the December 2024 offering 8-K (https://www.streetinsider.com/PRNewswire/Washington+Trust+Announces+Stock+Offering/24099511.html). EDGAR submissions feed (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0000737468.json) shows no filing of any kind after 2026-08-14.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR submissions feed for WASH: no 8-K, Form 4, 13D/G or prospectus supplement after the 2026-08-14 EFFECT; the only Form 4 since the Q2 print is the CEO's 0.907-share trust housekeeping sale on 2026-07-28 at $38.94 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/737468/000073746826000111/primary_01.xml), which bears on nothing.

Q2 10-Q Item 3 interest-rate sensitivity table (+/-100/200bp NII simulation): the main 10-Q document truncates at 100k characters in the fetch tool and the XBRL R-pages do not carry it, so WASH's own stated asset/liability sensitivity could not be read; finding 2 is therefore an inference rather than a company number.
Providence / Rhode Island office loan defaults or foreclosures in Q3 2026: nothing dated 2026 beyond the 2025 One Financial Plaza auction and the Providence Place mall (retail) receivership.
September 2026 MBA weekly application and rate data: search returned July 2026 and prior-year (2025) weeks only.
KRE / regional-bank weekly commentary for Oct 13-17, 2026: none found; price series were read directly instead (KRE flat on the week, CFG -0.1% and MTB -1.5% on their prints, INDB +3.6%).
Analyst actions on WASH since the Sept 16 Fed hike: none found (last actions KBW 2026-07-21, Seaport 2026-07-22).
Zacks ESP for the Q3 2026 quarter: not retrievable (page blocked; the indexed Zacks preview is for an older quarter).
Web search budget for this turn was exhausted after about 30 queries; the remaining checks were done by direct fetch of primary documents and price APIs.

baseline_tension: No skew to read (unusable chain); the findings agree with the 20-session drift (-6.2%, behind KRE) on fundamentals but the crowded short and the peer tape cut against it, which is why the findings sum negative and the scaled number stays close to zero.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (narrow proxy below a company number): finding 1 (peer deposit costs) resized -1.0 to -0.8 because it is three peers' numbers, not WASH's.
Rule 7 (crowded short shrinks a negative): finding 2 (Fed hike vs Q4 guide) resized -1.5 to -1.2 and p_up moved 45 to 46 on 7.34% of float short / 11.5 days to cover.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): finding 8 (the $150m shelf) resized -0.2 to -0.1 after answering what the money buys (nothing announced; routine three-year renewal).
Rule 8 (thin coverage moves more): abs_move_pct raised 7.0 to 7.5 on a 4-analyst name whose last three prints averaged a 12.6% absolute move.

Rules 1, 3, 6, 9 left findings 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 standing: the bar is two agreeing sources, finding 5 is stated as inside the guide, finding 3 is sized net of the clean rest of the book, and the positive positioning finding is kept beside the negatives because both can be true (a small miss into a crowded short).
